fix: anchor the credits pill to the permission-mode picker, not a DOM walk

The account-credits pill (the quota ring) used to be positioned by
walking up from the Usage control's current DOM position to find the
leftmost "material" sibling in the composer footer. That walk
re-resolved a different ancestor depending on whatever native DOM
happened to exist at the moment it ran — landing near the trailing
model/permission cluster on the first render pass (before the host
page's own toolbar had settled), then jumping to the leading "+"
button a few seconds later once it had. Users saw the pill render
next to "Bypass permissions" and then visibly relocate to its left.

Anchor credits directly to permissionModePicker.root instead — a
renderer-owned element that's inserted into the DOM at mount and only
moves under its own reconciliation. Credits now renders immediately to
the left of the permission-mode control from the first paint, grouped
with the other session/usage status indicators, and no longer depends
on where Usage happens to land.

- creditsPlacementAnchor(control) replaces the ancestor-walking version;
  drop the now-dead firstMaterialChild/attachControlWithin helpers.
- Split credits placement out of refreshUsagePlacement into its own
  refreshCreditsPlacement, decoupling it from Usage's anchor state.
- Reorder reconcileComposerNativeControls so the permission-mode
  picker's position is settled before credits anchors to it.
- renderer-credits-control: place() now inserts immediately *before*
  its anchor instead of after.

fix: clean up the Usage/Credits popover chrome for light theme

The shared popover chrome (Usage detail panel, Credits detail panel)
tinted its background by mixing 8% CanvasText into Canvas and paired
it with a deep 45px/0.35-alpha black shadow. That direction reads as
a correctly *lifted* dark elevated surface, but the same formula
muddies a light surface into flat grey and turns the oversized shadow
into a smudged halo instead of a crisp elevation cue — the "dirty"
look reported against the live light-theme screenshot.

Switch the fill, border, and both shadow layers to `light-dark()`,
which resolves off the same `color-scheme` that already drives
`Canvas`/`CanvasText` here (so it still tracks the host page's actual
theme, not the OS preference). Light gets a near-white surface with a
tight, low-opacity shadow; dark keeps the lifted-and-shadowed card.

feat: surface Antigravity quota and headless permission denials

Two gaps found by probing agy v1.1.22 directly.

Quota came from scraping the CLI log for the Language Server's random
HTTPS port and calling an undocumented gRPC method. The CLI answers
`/usage` itself, so it is unavailable on `--input-format stream-json`
but works as its own `--print=/usage` invocation, which returns a
structured `command_result` with one bucket per limit window. The
Adapter now reads that and exposes `credits()` / `refreshCredits()`,
which the Host Runtime already duck-types for the credits surface. The
Language Server path stays only for context-window usage, which
`/context` cannot serve because it is interactive-only.

Headless agy never asks the client to approve a tool: it applies its
own permission rules and reports a denial as a tool error, then ends
the Turn as SUCCESS with an empty response. That surfaced as a Turn
that silently did nothing. Tool items now carry the CLI's diagnostic,
and a Turn that only produced a denial fails with the effective agy
permission mode (read from the `init` event) and a pointer to the Skip
permissions Permission Mode. Turns that produced any assistant text
keep succeeding, so a partially denied Turn is unaffected.

The stream-json shapes and `parseAntigravityStreamLine` move to
`stream-events.ts` so the quota reader can decode the same envelope
without duplicating it.

fix: address review on Antigravity quota and denial diagnostics

[P1] Quota could stay blank forever. `externalAgentHasAccountCredits`
omitted antigravity, so once a Thread Usage inspection returned a
non-null usage the Renderer stopped retrying, while the Host only
kicks `refreshCredits()` asynchronously and reads the previous cache
in the same pass. Antigravity now joins the retry set, so the next
inspection picks up the landed quota.

[P1] The denial diagnostic echoed the rejected command line verbatim,

Same defect class, disclosed scope expansion: `normalizedProcessError`

authentication branch, where credentials are most likely — as the
error `message`. Both are sanitized now. This line predates the
feature but is the same leak in the same file.

buckets from the remaining side ("Weekly Limit Remaining") while
`AccountCreditsSnapshot` carries consumed percentages, so the popover
read "Five Hour Limit Remaining 1.46%" for 1.46% consumed. Labels are
now derived from the bucket window ("5-hour window", "Weekly window"),
keeping the label and the number on the same side. Values stay
consumed percentages, per the contract.

feat: expose Antigravity reasoning effort as Thinking selection

The Adapter declared `selectThinkingOption: false` on the grounds that
effort is baked into the Model ID and a separate axis would produce
invalid combinations. Probing the CLI shows the first half is true and
the conclusion is not:

    --model gemini-3.1-pro                   requires --effort (available: low, high)
    --model gemini-3.1-pro --effort low      -> gemini-3.1-pro-low
    --model gemini-3.1-pro-low --effort high conflicts with --effort=high
    --model gpt-oss-120b --effort high       invalid, only medium exists
    --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --effort high  invalid, no effort variants

Effort is a real second axis, just a per-Model one: each base Model
accepts its own subset and some accept none. `HarnessModel.supported
ThinkingOptionIds` already expresses exactly that, so the invalid
combinations the old reasoning worried about are prevented by the
Catalog rather than by hiding the capability.

`agy models` output is now grouped by base Model, the effort suffix
becomes a Thinking option, and `--effort` is passed as its own flag.
Selecting a Model that does not accept the retained effort drops it,
mirroring the Grok Adapter, so the CLI is never handed a combination it
rejects. A Model Ref that still carries an effort suffix comes from a
Thread stored before this change; the CLI accepts that form as long as
`--effort` is omitted, so existing Threads resume unchanged.

The Catalog projection moves into `model-catalog.ts`, matching the
other Adapters and keeping it out of an Adapter module already past 1100
lines.

The capability was declared but nothing transported the value, so the

argument either. Both encoders now take the effort and emit the same

reads it back, and one- and two-component carriers written before this
change still decode.

[P1] Restored Threads dropped it too. The CLI keeps no server-side
effort, so unlike Grok or OMP it cannot be recovered from live Session
state — it has to be replayed from the persisted carrier.
`ResumeSessionInput` gains a `thinkingOptionId` hint alongside the

fix(antigravity): read applied edit diffs from agy's Language Server

agy's stream-json publishes only `TargetFile` for `write_to_file` and
`replace_file_content` and keeps the file content out of the stream
entirely, so every patch the Host synthesized from those parameters was
empty. Codex Desktop cannot parse a body-less hunk and falls back to
rendering the git header itself as added lines, which is why every file
edit card showed `+4 -0` over `@@ -0,0 +0,0 @@` no matter what was
written, and the Turn summary card showed `+0 -0`.

Read the applied patch from agy's own Language Server instead: it records
each edit as a `CORTEX_STEP_TYPE_CODE_ACTION` carrying a line-typed
unified diff. The Adapter claims one Code Action per file-mutating step
and rebuilds Git hunks from it; a step whose patch cannot be read stays a
Tool Execution rather than showing an invented diff. Stream handling is
serialized per Turn so the awaited lookup cannot reorder Items.

Protocol Core stops emitting body-less patches, and republishes
`turn/diff/updated` when a File Change Item resolves its patch at
completion — without that the summary card kept its start-time value.

chore(renderer-extension): drop unused transcript status indicator and simulation script

The transcript status chip and injector lost their only call site when the
indicator was removed from the UI, but both modules, their two test files and
the event they listened for stayed in the tree. Nothing installs the injector,
so `codexhost:transcript-status` was dispatched to no listener and the
`detail` payload on `codexhost:renderer-adapter-status` went unread — its only
handler ignores the event argument and reads adapter state from its closure.

Restore the plain adapter status dispatch, delete the two modules and their
re-exports, and remove tools/run-simulation.mjs, which had no reference in any
npm script, tool or document.

test(antigravity): drop the full-pipeline simulation built on a stream agy cannot emit

The simulation fed write_to_file a CodeContent parameter and replace_file_content
a ReplacementContent parameter, then asserted the resulting +8/-1 diff. Real
`agy --output-format stream-json` publishes only TargetFile and strips edit
content entirely, which is why the applied patch now comes from the Language
Server instead; an Antigravity file tool no longer reaches fileChangeFromTool at
all. A failure here would have pointed at a branch Antigravity never takes.

Its remaining assertions are covered where the behaviour actually lives: the 1M
context window in antigravity-adapter, unquoted paths and command lines in
tool-projection and adversarial-stress, and the non-zero turn diff in
codex-ui-projector. It was also the only adapter test importing
@codexhost/protocol-core, which the package does not declare as a dependency and
which sits above the adapter layer.

fix: remove superseded Mapping Store lock files on startup

store.lock.stale-<ms> files are created by exactly one line - the rename
that moves a dead owner's lock aside before taking a new one - and
nothing in the repository ever removes them. They are not read back
either, so the directory grows by one file per run forever.

This is not a crash artefact but the normal path: close() releases the
lock only when it is reached, and the desktop Host Runtime installs no
SIGINT/SIGTERM handler, so a Node process terminated with the Desktop
process tree never runs its cleanup. A user who had been running the app
for a while had 14 of these, roughly one per session.

Widen the startup cleanup already running under the freshly acquired
lock to sweep them, including the one this run just created, and rename
it to match what it now does. Removal is best-effort, like the temp-file
sweep beside it.

Adding a signal handler to the main runtime path would be a separate
change with its own semantics (racing the existing stdin-EOF exit,
draining in-flight writes) and is deliberately not bundled here.

fix(linux): start managed Desktop in a new session

On Linux the managed Desktop was started with process_group(0): its own
process group, but still in the invoking terminal's session. From an
interactive terminal it was therefore a background job, and an
interactive shell spawned during Desktop startup stopped the whole group
via job control (SIGTTIN), so the Controller never became ready.

Start the Desktop with setsid(2) instead. The child still leads its own
process group (PGID == PID), so launch ownership and cleanup are
unchanged, but it has no controlling terminal that job control could use
to suspend it. This matches the reported `setsid --fork --wait` workaround.

fix(hermes): unshard warm transports across working directories

Desktop gives every Thread a unique cwd (~/Documents/Codex/<date>/<name>),
so the cwd-keyed warm scope never matched a new Thread's open: every
freshly named session paid the full cold start (spawn + initialize +
session/new), which users feel as 'some new sessions take forever'.

Hermes derives all session cwd behavior from the session/new parameter
(agent.session_cwd, per-task env overrides, turn-time session vars) and
never from the process cwd, so a warm transport is safe to reuse across
directories: drop cwd from the warm scope and retarget the transport to
the requesting directory before opening. Environment still scopes the
pool, and the inspection cache (model catalog) is cwd-independent.

fix(host-runtime): keep a Subagent Thread active while its Subagent runs

A Subagent Thread was reported as active exactly once, in the
`thread/started` payload emitted by `#materializeSubagent`. Opening that
Thread went through `ExternalThreadRuntime.register()`, which hardcodes
`running: false` and publishes a Thread value built without `running`, so
Codex was told `{"type":"idle"}` while the Subagent was still working.
`#setSubagentThreadStatus` could not repair it either: the Host's own view
had not changed, so its `previousStatus === status` guard kept it silent.

Seed `running` in `register()` from the Host's tracked Subagent status and
publish the Thread value with that status, so opening a running Subagent
Thread no longer downgrades it. Non-Subagent Threads are unaffected: the
callback returns false for every Thread the Host is not tracking.

fix(renderer): mount settings trigger before native header actions

The application-header settings trigger anchored on the right-most
`header-shell-slot`, which is the window-layout slot to the right of the
header context menu surface. The trigger therefore rendered after every
native control the surface owns, contrary to the extensible-settings-shell
requirement that it be the first control in the right-side action group,
and it displaced native controls whenever its own width changed.

Anchor on the native action group instead: the trailing
`[data-app-shell-header-obstacle="true"]` child of the header context menu
surface. The right-most `header-shell-slot` stays as the fallback for the
blank-Thread case where no native action group is rendered. Because the
anchor is a native element rather than an ordinal position, the trigger
also keeps its place when another extension inserts a control before it.

fix(codebuddy): tolerate a Tool result recorded before its call

A native history whose Tool result precedes its call failed the whole read
with `Native Tool result has no call`, leaving the Thread unusable: every
history snapshot, and therefore every new message, was rejected until the
user resumed the Native Session in the CLI instead.

CodeBuddy persists a call and its result from separate writers. A call that
is refused before it runs (for example a command blocked by CodeBuddy's own
security check) records its result without waiting for the call row, so the
parent chain can carry the result first. Observed once in 793 Tool pairs
across the local CodeBuddy history; the two rows were written 5 ms apart.

Hold such a result and apply it when its call arrives, keeping one Item per
call. A result whose call never appears cannot be attributed to a renderable
Tool and is dropped instead of failing the read; other damaged history still
produces an explicit error.

OMP servers gate subagent_lifecycle/subagent_progress/subagent_event

delegation projection, child Thread materialization, and Desktop panel

after negotiate_protocol; builds without the command reject it and
degrade gracefully. The test fake now models the server-side gate
(silent until subscribed, plus an unsupported mode) instead of pushing
frames unconditionally, and two regression tests pin the subscription
and the degraded path.

OMP's RPC subagent registry is in-memory and only populated by live
task events, so a cold --resume process cannot resolve a completed

subagent or session file unavailable'. The adapter's readSnapshot
spawned such a cold process for every child Thread read, so clicking

even though OMP persists it next to the parent Session file.

validate the ID as a plain file name, cap at 8 MiB, and require the
resolved file to stay inside its parent Session directory. Fall back
to the RPC path only when no transcript file exists, preserving the
previous behavior for other layouts. Verified against a real OMP
session: the cold RPC path fails, the file path returns the full
turn/items snapshot in milliseconds.

Address review feedback: the stat check is point-in-time and a live
OMP process can append to the transcript after it. Pass the byte
limit into readOmpSessionHistory so the read stream itself stops at
MAX_SUBAGENT_TRANSCRIPT_BYTES regardless of concurrent writes.
